data_sources.Source: AWS Terrain Tiles, Terrarium PNG, zoom 8: `https://s3.amazonaws.com/elevation-tiles-prod/terrarium/{z}/{x}/{y}.png` (1,224 tiles). Height = R·256 + G + B/256 − 32768.
NASA POWER Climatology API v2.10.1, `https://power.larc.nasa.gov/api/temporal/climatology/point`, community AG, parameters `T2M`, `T2M_MAX`, `T2M_MIN`, `PRECTOTCORR`, one call per cell center
data_sources.Resolution used: Native ≈ 0.5° (MERRA-2 / 0.5° grid), queried at 1° cell centers

data_sources.Source: MOLA MEGDR global DEM mosaic, 463 m, USGS Astrogeology: `https://planetarymaps.usgs.gov/mosaic/Mars_MGS_MOLA_DEM_mosaic_global_463m.tif` (redirects to `https://asc-pds-services.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/mosaic/Mars_MGS_MOLA_DEM_mosaic_global_463m.tif`). File is 2.1 GB, so only the Jezero window was read via HTTP range requests (no full download).
data_sources.Resolution used: 463.09 m/px N–S, 439.4 m/px E–W (true ground, equirectangular scaled by cos 18.4°); crop 154×192 px

citations: Terrain tiles: "Terrain Tiles (Terrarium), Mapzen / Amazon Web Services Open Data Registry, `https://registry.opendata.aws/terrain-tiles/`. Includes data from SRTM, ASTER GDEM, GMTED2010, and others; see `https://github.com/tilezen/joerd/blob/master/docs/attribution.md`."

Climate: "NASA Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources (POWER) Project, NASA Langley Research Center, `https://power.larc.nasa.gov/`, accessed November 2026 (Climatology API v2.10.1; MERRA-2 and CERES/GEOS-derived meteorology)."

Mars: "Smith, D. E., et al. (2001), Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter: Experiment summary after the first year of global mapping of Mars, J. Geophys. Res., 106(E10), 23689–23722. Mars MGS MOLA DEM 463 m/pix mosaic, USGS Astrogeology Science Center, `https://astrogeology.usgs.gov/search/map/mars_mgs_mola_dem_463m`."
changelog: We now flag likely water cells (flat sea or lake surface, or deep sea floor) from elevation and slope, and leave them unscored.
310 of 1,960 cells were flagged as water; percentiles, candidates and disagreements now use land cells only.
Before the fix, the three "disagreement" cells were Caspian Sea water; the Run 1 outputs are archived for comparison.
The environment score is still aridity-only until Mars climate values are entered, and temperature range means hottest-month max minus coldest-month min.
Coastal cells that mix land and water may not be flagged, and the validation (6 points) is exploratory, not statistical proof.
